# Show Me the Counts (SMTC)

> Show Me the Counts is a free mobile app for dancers that turns any song into a structured practice tool. Import your own music, mark and name specific sections, loop them on repeat, adjust playback speed from 50% to 150%, and isolate individual instruments using AI-powered stem separation. Built for bachata, salsa, kizomba, zouk, and any dance style.

## Links

- [Homepage](https://showmethecounts.com/): Landing page with features, founder story, FAQ, and download links
- [Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.smtc.mobile): Android app listing
- [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/showmethecounts/): Official Instagram account

## Key Facts

- **Category**: Music / Dance Practice
- **Platform**: Android (iOS coming soon)
- **Price**: Free with optional Pro subscription ($4.99/month)
- **Pro Trial**: 7-day free trial
- **Package ID**: com.smtc.mobile

## Core Features (Free)

- Section creation: Mark, name, and color-code any part of a song
- Smart looping: Loop any section seamlessly for focused repetition
- Speed control: Adjust playback from 50% to 150%
- Offline playback: Works with local music files

## Pro Features

- Stem separation: AI-powered isolation of vocals, bass, drums, and melody
- Unlimited sections per track
- Custom tags for organizing sections
- Section sharing: Share specific sections with other dancers or students

## Target Audience

- Social dancers (bachata, salsa, kizomba, zouk, and all styles)
- Freestyle dancers training musicality and groove
- Choreographers and performance teams drilling routines
- Dance instructors preparing class music and building annotated song libraries

## What Problem It Solves

Most dancers practice by playing a full song and freestyling. SMTC enables deliberate, targeted practice — looping the exact 8-count where you need to be sharper, slowing down a section to understand the feel, or isolating the bass line to train rhythmic awareness. It bridges the gap between knowing moves and knowing when to use them.
